description: Backend prediction cache + CloudWatch metrics (Issue #23 criteria 1 and 2, plus proposal c metrics). Cache the full mode:'prediction' PredictionResponse (favorite, probability, narrative, model, generatedAt, metrics) in DynamoDB keyed by seriesId + series situation (high.wins-low.wins) + language + model id + accuracy, so the SECOND and later requests for the SAME situation are served from cache WITHOUT calling predict()/Bedrock, and a change in the win counts (a game result update) yields a different key => a fresh Bedrock call (effective invalidation). Emit CloudWatch metrics for cache hit/miss and Bedrock InvokeModel count via Embedded Metric Format (EMF) log lines (no new IAM required). All AWS mocked in tests. This is the core billable-path change; it sits in BracketService.getPrediction AFTER the existing results-only / series-final / unresolvable-or-not-started short-circuits (those never call Bedrock, so they are not cached).
steps: Add a pure, deterministic cache-key function. Create backend/src/service/predictionCacheKey.ts exporting `predictionCacheKey(input: { seriesId: string; highWins: number; lowWins: number; language: NarrativeLanguage; modelId: string; accuracy: number }): string` returning `PREDICTION#<seriesId>#<highWins>-<lowWins>#<language>#<modelId>#<accuracy>`. Normalize accuracy to a stable string (e.g. the resolved numeric default when undefined) so the same logical situation always maps to the same key. Keep it pure (no I/O). Document the format in a JSDoc block. Add backend/src/service/predictionCacheKey.test.ts covering: deterministic/stable output for identical inputs, DIFFERENT key when ANY component changes (seriesId, highWins, lowWins, language, modelId, accuracy) - the win-count variation is the criterion-2 invalidation proof at the key level.

Extend the DynamoDB store. In backend/src/store/dynamo.ts: add a `PREDICTION_TTL_SECONDS` constant (choose a sane backstop, e.g. 60*15 = 15 minutes, matching the live/bracket cadence; document why - the win-count key already invalidates on series progress, the TTL is only a safety backstop against stale situations), add a `predictionPartitionKey(cacheKey: string)` helper (the key is already the full PREDICTION#... string, so this can be identity or wrap it), add `getCachedPrediction(cacheKey: string): Promise<PredictionResponse | undefined>` and `putCachedPrediction(cacheKey: string, response: PredictionResponse, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<void>` to the DynamoBracketStore class AND to the BracketStore interface. Follow the existing GAME#<gamePk> helpers exactly: GetCommand/PutCommand on the single-pk table, store under `pk`, carry numeric `ttl`, return undefined / no-op when TABLE_NAME is unset. Only cache mode:'prediction' responses.

Wire the cache into BracketService.getPrediction (backend/src/service/bracketService.ts). AFTER the results-only short-circuit, the series-final short-circuit, and the unresolvable/not-started short-circuit (leave all three BEFORE the cache - they do not call Bedrock), and AFTER resolving the model id and language (so the key uses the resolved values), BEFORE calling resolveWinPct/predict/generateNarrative: build the cache key with predictionCacheKey({ seriesId, highWins: series.high.wins, lowWins: series.low.wins, language: resolvedLanguage, modelId: resolvedModel, accuracy: resolvedAccuracy }). Note accuracy may be undefined at the service boundary; resolve it to the model default used by predict() so the key is stable (pick the same default predict() applies, e.g. 0.5, and use that constant in the key). Call store.getCachedPrediction(key): on HIT emit a cache-hit metric and RETURN the cached response immediately (predict() and generateNarrative() MUST NOT run). On MISS emit a cache-miss metric, run the existing predict()+generateNarrative() path, assemble the mode:'prediction' response exactly as today, write it with store.putCachedPrediction(key, response), and return it. Keep seriesId resolution via resolveSeries and the favorite/underdog/metrics assembly unchanged.

Add an EMF metrics helper. Create backend/src/metrics/emf.ts exporting a small function (e.g. `emitPredictionMetric(kind: 'hit' | 'miss')` and `emitBedrockInvokeMetric(count: number)`, or a single `emitCacheMetric({ cacheResult: 'hit'|'miss', bedrockInvocations: number })`) that writes ONE CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format JSON object to stdout via console.log. Use a documented namespace (e.g. `MlbPostseason/Prediction`) and metric names (e.g. `PredictionCacheHit`, `PredictionCacheMiss`, `BedrockInvokeCount`). The _aws EMF envelope must list the namespace, the metric name(s), and no high-cardinality dimensions (keep seriesId out of dimensions to avoid metric explosion; it may go in the log body as a property, not a dimension). Make it side-effect-only (writes to stdout) and injectable/mockable (allow passing a sink defaulting to console.log) so a unit test can assert the emitted shape without spying on console. Export metric name/namespace constants for reuse and documentation.

Call the metrics helper from getPrediction: emit a hit metric (and BedrockInvokeCount 0) on a cache hit, and a miss metric (and BedrockInvokeCount 1, since generateNarrative is the single InvokeModel attempt) on a cache miss. Note generateNarrative falls back deterministically on Bedrock error but still represents one invoke attempt; count the attempt. Keep metric emission non-throwing so it never breaks the response (wrap in try/catch or make the sink safe).

Add backend/src/metrics/emf.test.ts: assert the helper emits exactly one JSON line with the correct namespace, metric name(s), unit, and values for both hit and miss, using an injected sink (array push) rather than the real console.

Extend backend/src/service/bracketService.test.ts: (a) update the in-memory memoryStore() mock to implement the two NEW BracketStore methods getCachedPrediction/putCachedPrediction (back them with a Map or a single slot keyed by the cache key; vi.fn so calls can be asserted). (b) Criterion 1 test: build a current-season (2026) predictable, started, non-final series (status 'in_progress' with at least one decided game or wins > 0 so hasStartedSeries is true). Inject a BedrockInvoker mock whose invoke is a vi.fn. Call getPrediction twice with the SAME (seriesId, season, accuracy, language, model). Assert: first call => invoker.invoke called exactly once AND putCachedPrediction called once; second call => invoker.invoke call count UNCHANGED (still 1, i.e. ZERO additional Bedrock calls) and the response equals the first (served from cache). (c) Criterion 2 test: with a cache seeded by a first call, change the series win counts (e.g. advance high.wins by 1 to simulate a game result update) OR change the resolved key input, call getPrediction again, and assert invoker.invoke is called AGAIN (a fresh Bedrock call) because the key changed. Mock resolveWinPct inputs by injecting winPct via deps so predict() is deterministic. Keep all existing tests passing (the memoryStore signature change must be backward compatible with current getBracket/getGameDetail tests).
acceptance_criteria: backend/src/service/predictionCacheKey.ts exists as a pure function and predictionCacheKey.test.ts proves the key is stable for identical inputs and changes when any of seriesId/highWins/lowWins/language/modelId/accuracy changes

DynamoBracketStore and the BracketStore interface expose getCachedPrediction/putCachedPrediction following the GAME#<gamePk> pattern, with a PREDICTION_TTL_SECONDS backstop and TABLE_NAME-unset graceful degradation
A service test proves criterion 1: a 2nd request for the same situation returns the cached response and makes ZERO additional Bedrock invoke calls
A service test proves criterion 2: changing the series win counts produces a fresh Bedrock invoke call (cache effectively invalidated by the key)
An EMF metrics helper emits cache hit/miss and Bedrock invoke-count metrics to stdout with a documented namespace and metric names, and its unit test asserts the emitted shape via an injected sink
The cache sits AFTER the results-only/series-final/not-started short-circuits (those paths still never call predict/Bedrock and are not cached)
npm run build and npm test pass with all new and existing tests green
verification: npm test (exit 0; new predictionCacheKey, emf, and the two bracketService criterion tests pass)
findings: Implemented pure predictionCacheKey (PREDICTION#<seriesId>#<highWins>-<lowWins>#<language>#<modelId>#<accuracy>) with undefined accuracy resolved to DEFAULT_ACCURACY (0.5) from @mlb/shared for a stable key. Added getCachedPrediction/putCachedPrediction to BracketStore interface + DynamoBracketStore (PREDICTION_TTL_SECONDS=15min backstop, TABLE_NAME-unset graceful degradation, only caches mode:'prediction'). Cache wraps the billable branch in getPrediction AFTER the results-only/final/not-started short-circuits and AFTER resolving model/language/accuracy. EMF helper in backend/src/metrics/emf.ts (namespace MlbPostseason/Prediction, metrics PredictionCacheHit/PredictionCacheMiss/BedrockInvokeCount, no high-cardinality dimensions, injectable sink, non-throwing). Extended memoryStore mock with the two new methods (Map-backed). New tests: predictionCacheKey.test.ts (7), emf.test.ts (3), and three cache criterion tests in bracketService.test.ts. npm run build and npm test both exit 0; backend 124 tests pass, all existing tests green. No infra/docs changes (out of scope for FEAT-002). The service uses the default console.log sink for metrics so EMF lines appear in test stdout; this is expected and harmless.
